title: Nexus
description: Full-stack project management application with authentication, task tracking, Kanban board, and analytics. Built with Next.js App Router, Server Actions, and Prisma.

caseStudy.projectOverview: Nexus is a full-stack project management application built with Next.js 15 App Router. It covers authentication (Google OAuth and email/password), task and project management, a Kanban board, and an analytics dashboard with charts. It started as a client-only frontend consuming an external REST API and has since moved to a server-first architecture using Server Components, Server Actions, and Prisma ORM, which made it a real migration exercise as much as a product.
whyThisStack: Next.js App Router enables Server Components and Server Actions, which removed the need for a separate API layer and a client-side state management library
Prisma ORM provides type-safe database access that integrates cleanly with TypeScript and keeps schema and queries in sync
Auth.js v5 handles the full authentication lifecycle (sessions, OAuth, and credentials) with Edge-compatible middleware for route protection
A centralised ActionResult type with Zod validation keeps Server Actions consistent, with errors surfaced to the UI in a uniform pattern
keyFeatures: Google OAuth and email/password authentication with password reset flow and rate limiting
Database queries scoped by user to keep each account's data isolated
Task management with filtering, pagination, tagging, and status tracking
Analytics dashboard with priority distribution and tasks-by-status charts
Reusable Server Actions with a centralised ActionResult type and Zod validation
challengesTradeoffs: Migrating incrementally from React Query and Axios to Server Actions without breaking existing features
Designing a scalable actions architecture, splitting monolithic files into co-located per-action modules with tests
Balancing server-side simplicity with client interactivity by using the 'use client' boundary carefully
nextSteps: Explore SaaS foundations: multi-user workspaces and billing

title: Redirect Lab
description: Full-stack link management platform with custom short URLs, access tracking, cross-tab synchronisation, accessible interactions, infinite scrolling, and CSV export through Cloudflare R2.

caseStudy.projectOverview: Redirect Lab is a full-stack link management platform built with an independent React client and Fastify API. It evolved from an earlier project and was rebuilt with a new identity, independently deployable repositories, stronger accessibility and testing practices, and a cost-conscious cloud architecture. The goal was to turn a basic URL shortener into a maintainable portfolio product with a focused user experience, reliable state handling, automated quality checks, and infrastructure that can run at little or no cost.
whyThisStack: React and TanStack Query provide a focused client architecture with explicit server-state caching, mutation feedback, and paginated data loading
Fastify and Drizzle ORM create a lightweight, type-safe API and persistence layer that stays aligned with the TypeScript domain model
Vitest, Testing Library, and axe-core support fast behavioral and accessibility testing without adding external testing services
Vercel, Railway, Neon, and Cloudflare R2 provide independently deployable infrastructure with practical free or low-cost tiers
keyFeatures: Custom short URL creation with validation and duplicate prevention
Cross-tab access count synchronisation through BroadcastChannel, without additional real-time infrastructure
Paginated link loading with infinite scrolling and IntersectionObserver
CSV export stored on Cloudflare R2 and delivered through a public URL
Accessible forms, dialogs, controls, and focus states, with automated axe checks
challengesTradeoffs: Separating the original monorepo while preserving history and letting the client and API evolve independently
Replacing the original AWS delivery setup with lower-cost services without losing deployment reliability
Keeping access counts synchronised across tabs without adding WebSockets or an external real-time service
Protecting delivery scope by postponing authentication and advanced analytics until the core product was stable
nextSteps: Build an access analytics dashboard with clicks grouped by period
Add QR Code generation and PNG download
